nodes.author: SSsagarHyd
nodes.text: Insufficient Health Infrastructure: India's healthcare system was ill-prepared for the pandemic. Hospitals faced severe shortages of beds, oxygen, and essential medical supplies during the second wave in 2021.

nodes.author: SSsagarHyd
nodes.text: Vaccine Policy Missteps: The initial vaccine rollout was slow and uncoordinated. Delays in securing adequate vaccine supplies and inconsistent policies on vaccine distribution and pricing added to the chaos.

nodes.author: SSsagarHyd
nodes.text:
Underreporting of Cases and Deaths:
There were widespread allegations of underreporting COVID-19 cases and deaths. The official numbers often did not match independent reports or observations, raising concerns about transparency and accountability.

nodes.author: SSsagarHyd
nodes.text:
Economic Impact and Insufficient Relief Measures:
The lockdown and subsequent waves of the pandemic severely impacted the economy, leading to job losses. Critics argued that the relief measures announced by the government were inadequate and did not reach the most vulnerable.

nodes.author: SSsagarHyd
nodes.text: The handling of the COVID-19 pandemic by the Modi government has been a subject of intense debate and criticism. While the challenges were unprecedented, the failures in planning, communication, and execution exacerbated the crisis, impacting millions of lives across the country
